Australian made, distributed nationally. 25 year guarantee Backed by our patented, fully engineered system. Supply only or installed Flat-pack for your team, or fully installed by ours. Overview Gallery Downloads Reviews FAQ Overview MDF staircases. Designed the way builders need them. Fast, solid and strong stairs. Our Easy MDF stair range offers the fastest and most reliable stairs available. It’s why they have been used in hundreds of thousands of homes by builders of all sizes for over forty years. Using our unique patented dovetail system our stairs are manufactured to exacting measurements so minimal cutting is needed on site, making it quick and easy to install. With warehousing around Australia and a central manufacturing facility, we take pride in offering the fastest delivery of stairs possible. We provide a range of installation options, including using one of our installation teams or doing it yourself with our handy guides. On larger and regional developments we can provide training to your carpenters on how to install the stairs. Specifications Material MDF - moisture resistant grade Finish options DIY carpet, hybrid, vinyl, timber, tiled Riser options Closed Balustrade Glass, timber, metal, stainless - all compatible Warranty 25 year manufacturing guarantee Standards NCC compliant Install at frame stage.Save time. Save money. Stairlock’s Easy MDF system goes in at frame stage, before plastering, using our moisture-resistant E0 grade board. On volume residential and townhouse developments that’s an advantage: a fast, repeatable install on every lot, on top of the standard 25-year MDF guarantee. MDF stairs are staircases constructed using engineered medium-density fibreboard components, typically used in residential construction as a cost-effective and consistent alternative to solid timber. They are most commonly installed in volume-built homes where speed, repeatability, and uniform finishes are important. MDF staircases are particularly well suited to townhouses, duplexes and terraces. Do MDF stairs need to be finished, and what are the options? Yes. MDF staircases always require a final finish. Common options include carpet, hybrid flooring, timber overlays, tiles, and in some cases paint systems designed specifically for MDF substrates. The choice usually depends on the project specification and desired aesthetic, but most volume residential builds use carpet or fully covered finishes to seamlessly match or complement the selected flooring system throughout the home. How do MDF stairs compare to timber stairs? MDF stairs offer greater consistency in manufacturing, reduced variation between components, and typically faster installation in volume residential builds. They are particularly well suited to townhouses, duplexes and terrace homes where repeatable outcomes, speed, and cost efficiency are key. Timber stairs are often preferred for high-end architectural or feature applications where natural material variation and bespoke detailing are a priority. However, MDF stair systems can also be specified alongside timber elements, for example hardwood stringers, handrails, or balustrade components allow you to achieve a more premium aesthetic while retaining the efficiency and consistency of an MDF structural system. How are MDF staircases installed? MDF stair systems are typically prefabricated to precise measurements and installed as a complete system on site, reducing the need for extensive cutting or adjustment. This improves installation speed and consistency, particularly in new home construction environments such as townhouses, duplexes and other volume residential builds. At Stairlock, we also offer the option to install your MDF staircase prior to gyprock or plasterboard. This allows trades earlier access to upper levels, improving site safety and overall construction productivity. Do MDF stairs meet Australian building standards? Yes. MDF stair systems can be designed and manufactured to meet the relevant parts of the NCC (National Construction Code) and Australian Standards for residential stair construction. As with all staircases, compliance depends on the overall design, accurate measurements, and how the staircase is installed as part of the finished build. This is typically managed by the builder or building designer within the wider project. At Stairlock, we supply engineered MDF stair systems and can also provide full installation where required. The overlay is a real oak surface laid over a solid engineered MDF core. You get the same oak look as solid timber, in a lighter build that costs less. The hardwood is solid timber the whole way through, so it’s the premium option, and it can be sanded back and refinished several times over its life where the overlay can’t. Is American Oak overlay real oak? Yes. The overlay is a real layer of American Oak over an MDF core, so the surface you see and touch is oak, with the same grain and the same stain options as solid timber. It isn’t a printed or laminate lookalike. The core underneath just keeps it stable and brings the cost down. Can American Oak stairs be sanded back and refinished? It depends on the build. Solid American Oak hardwood can be sanded right back and refinished three to five times over its life, so the staircase can be brought back to new decades later. The overlay can’t be sanded back the same way, since the oak surface is a thin real layer over the core. You can still refresh it with a clean and a new coat of finish, but if being able to fully resand it matters to you, go with solid. Can American Oak be stained to match my floor? Yes. American Oak takes stain evenly where a lot of timbers blotch, so it’s straightforward for your painter or finisher to match it to the floor, or take it lighter or darker. We supply the staircase ready to finish, and both overlay and solid have a real oak surface, so they take colour the same way. The staining and sealing is done on site by your finisher. Do you make balustrades and handrails in American Oak too? Yes. We’ve got a range of American Oak balusters and handrails in different profiles to suit your design, along with matching posts, so the same oak can run through the whole balustrade and rail, not just the stairs. How much does an American Oak staircase cost? It comes down to the staircase. The main things that move the price are the design and size, which build you go with, and how much of it is done in oak.
